title: Complex numbers
overview: Revise Argand diagrams, modulus/argument, polar form. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Use Cartesian and polar forms, modulus, argument and conjugates.
Perform arithmetic and use conjugate-pair roots for real polynomials.
Multiply/divide in polar form and find exact square roots.
Represent equations and inequalities as loci on an Argand diagram.

definitions.definition: z=x+iy, where i²=−1 and x,y are real.
arg z is the directed angle from the positive real axis to z.
A plane with real part horizontally and imaginary part vertically.

sections.title: Cartesian arithmetic
content: Add real and imaginary parts separately and use i²=−1 when multiplying. To divide by c+id, multiply numerator and denominator by c−id so the denominator becomes c²+d². Equality requires both real parts and imaginary parts to match.
bullets: Real-coefficient polynomial roots occur in conjugate pairs.

sections.title: Polar form
content: Write z=r(cosθ+i sinθ), where r=|z| and θ=arg z. On multiplication, multiply moduli and add arguments; on division, divide moduli and subtract arguments. Give the argument in the interval requested.
bullets: Use atan2 thinking or a sketch to choose the correct quadrant.

sections.title: Square roots and equations
content: For w²=z, let w=a+ib and compare real and imaginary parts, using a²+b²=|z| as a second relation. The two roots are opposites. For polynomial questions, include the conjugate of any given non-real root, form the quadratic factor and divide.
bullets: Show exact Cartesian working for square roots.
Check by squaring the final roots.

sections.title: Loci
content: |z−a|=r is a circle centred at a; |z−a|<r is its interior. |z−a|=|z−b| is the perpendicular bisector of AB. arg(z−a)=α is a ray from a, with the initial point excluded.
bullets: Use solid or dashed boundaries to distinguish inclusive and strict inequalities.
Shade only after testing a simple point.

examTips: Draw a small Argand sketch before fixing an argument quadrant.
For loci, label centre, radius, boundary inclusion and excluded points.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using arctan(y/x) without correcting the quadrant.
Forgetting that square roots occur as ±w.
Drawing arg(z−a)=α as a full line instead of a ray.

quickRecall.question: Why multiply by a conjugate when dividing?
quickRecall.answer: It makes the denominator real because (c+id)(c−id)=c²+d².

quickRecall.question: What locus is |z−a|=r?
quickRecall.answer: A circle centred at a with radius r.

quickRecall.question: What happens to arguments when complex numbers are divided?
quickRecall.answer: Subtract the divisor's argument from the numerator's argument.
